articles.title: ToneTag Launches India's First In-Car Fuel Payments on TATA.CARS via UPI Circle & IndianOil
articles.content: ToneTag has launched India’s first In-Car Fuel Payment solution at Global Fintech Fest (GFF) 2026, using an IoT-enabled implementation of NPCI’s UPI Circle framework for TATA.CARS’ DrivePay solution in collaboration with IndianOil. The solution enables customers to securely pay for fuel at IndianOil outlets. DrivePay, powered by ToneTag, extends digital payments into connected vehicles, allowing customers to complete fuel payments through their vehicle’s interface after refuelling, without using a separate mobile application, card or other payment method. Following its launch at GFF 2026, the solution is being deployed in collaboration with IndianOil to enable an In-Car Fuel Payment experience at IndianOil Retail Outlets, with a formal rollout expected in the coming months. The solution leverages NPCI’s UPI Circle framework, “Introduction of IoT Devices and Software on the UPI Ecosystem” , with ToneTag providing the technology layer that enables the IoT-based payment experience. By integrating the payment capability into the connected vehicle, DrivePay creates a secure, convenient and contactless way for customers to pay for fuel directly from their vehicle. The solution will also integrate IndianOil’s XTRAREWARDS loyalty programme, enabling eligible customers to earn reward points without sharing their mobile number during the transaction. The collaboration brings together IndianOil’s extensive fuel retail network, TATA.CARS’ connected vehicle ecosystem, ToneTag’s payment technology and NPCI’s digital payments infrastructure, creating a foundation for wider applications across in-vehicle payments, commerce and digital services. Following the successful implementation of DrivePay with TATA.CARS, ToneTag is not stopping here. The company sees a broader opportunity to extend its payment technology across the connected mobility ecosystem and will explore opportunities to work with other automotive OEMs and mobility ecosystem players to enable similar in-vehicle payment and commerce experiences. “Payments are rapidly moving beyond traditional interfaces such as cards and smartphones, and connected devices are emerging as the next frontier for commerce. With DrivePay, powered by ToneTag, we are bringing an IoT-based UPI Circle payment experience directly into the connected vehicle. This initiative with IndianOil, TATA.CARS and NPCI demonstrates how payment infrastructure can seamlessly extend into connected devices, enabling the vehicle itself to become a secure payment interface. We believe this is an important step towards a future where mobility, payments and commerce are seamlessly connected,” said Vivek Kumar Singh, Co-Founder and Director – Labs, ToneTag. With its connected car solution, ToneTag is bringing payments closer to where consumers interact with their vehicles, creating new possibilities for seamless and connected commerce experiences.

articles.title: QClairvoyance Quantum Labs signs MoU with Samgnya for quantum technology development
articles.content: NRI View Point cartoon My Space Reviews Education Today Property Lifestyle Home | Hyderabad | Qclairvoyance Quantum Labs Signs Mou With Samgnya For Quantum Technology Development QClairvoyance Quantum Labs signs MoU with Samgnya for quantum technology development QClairvoyance Quantum Labs has signed an MoU with IITM–C-DOT Samgnya Technologies Foundation to collaborate on Quantum Computing, Quantum Algorithms, Quantum AI, Post-Quantum Cybersecurity and next-generation computing, with a focus on research, technology development, validation and deployment By Telangana Today Published Date - 11 September 2026, 04:12 PM Hyderabad: QClairvoyance Quantum Labs has signed an MoU with IITM–C-DOT Samgnya Technologies Foundation, India’s National Hub for Quantum Communication, established under the National Quantum Mission (NQM) of the Department of Science & Technology. The collaboration will focus on Quantum Computing, Quantum Algorithms, Quantum AI, Post-Quantum Cybersecurity and next-generation computing, with an emphasis on research, technology development, validation and eventual deployment. Samgnya serves as a national platform bringing together research, technology, testbeds, industry, startups and talent to accelerate India’s quantum technology ecosystem. Its mandate spans advanced R&D, quantum communication and Quantum Key Distribution (QKD), technology translation and validation, national testbeds, industry collaboration, startup incubation, capability and skill development, standards and interoperability, technology transfer and commercialisation. Colonel Sai Shankar P, VSM (Retd.), Founder of QClairvoyance Quantum Labs, said, “What makes this collaboration particularly meaningful for us is the opportunity to work across research, technology validation, testbeds, industry collaboration, talent development and, ultimately, technology translation and commercialisation.” Ravindra Barlingay, CEO of IITM–C-DOT Samgnya Technologies Foundation, said, “Quantum technology will create meaningful impact only when we are able to translate strong research and innovation into technologies that are validated, trusted and deployable at scale.” Follow Us : Tags quantum AI Quantum Computing Quantum Cybersecurity quantum technology Related News University of Melbourne partners with TIDCO to build emerging tech hub in Tamil Nadu Amaravati Quantum Valley building world-class quantum ecosystem: Chandrababu Naidu Chandrababu Naidu launches India’s first quantum testbeds in Amaravati Andhra Pradesh: Chandrababu Naidu to launch India’s first indigenous quantum computers in Amaravati Latest News QClairvoyance Quantum Labs signs MoU with Samgnya for quantum technology development 5 seconds ago Hyderabad couple allegedly loses Rs 1.97 crore in real estate fraud 6 minutes ago Governor Shiv Pratap Shukla urges people to opt for clay Ganesha idols 12 minutes ago ‘I will need to come with all energy’: Rybakina on Sabalenka US Open final 25 minutes ago Iran President Masoud Pezeshkian arrives in Delhi for BRICS Summit 32 minutes ago NNRG’s ECE department gets NBA Tier-I accreditation 39 minutes ago Anemia levels in adolescent girls of Telangana dropped by 15 percent without a single visit to hospital, ICMR study 45 minutes ago Heavy rain, thunderstorms likely across Telangana over weekend 1 hour ago

articles.title: ISRO successfully tests CE20 cryogenic engine for LVM3-M7 mission - Manorama Yearbook
articles.content: • ISRO successfully conducted the flight acceptance hot testing of the cryogenic engine identified for the seventh operational mission of the LVM3 launch vehicle (LVM3-M7). • The test was conducted at the Main Engine & stage Test facility (MET) at ISRO Propulsion Complex (IPRC), Mahendragiri. • LVM3, formerly known as GSLV MkIII, is ISRO’s heaviest rocket and uses the CE20 cryogenic engine to power its upper stage. How was the test conducted? • Cryogenic engines for every mission undergo hot testing as part of its acceptance for the flight. • In order to conduct hot testing of this upper stage engine under sea-level conditions with its nozzle designed for high altitude operations, a Nozzle Protection System (NPS) was developed and validated previously through multiple qualification tests. • NPS has reduced the time and effort associated with flight acceptance testing of cryogenic engines, simulating the flight equivalent vacuum conditions at High Altitude Test Facility. • In order to enhance the payload capability of the LVM3 vehicle, future missions of LVM3 are planned with C32 stage operating at an uprated thrust level of 22t for the CE20 engine. • In view of this, the flight acceptance test was conducted at 22t thrust level. • Performance of the CE20 engine met all the test objectives which confirmed satisfactory performance of the engine systems. • The same test demonstrated the performance of a LOX Tank Pressurisation Module (LTPM) designed for the C32 stage, an upgraded cryogenic upper stage planned for India’s Gaganyaan missions. • The engine will be refurbished and assembled to the C32 flight stage for LVM3-M7 mission which is scheduled during the fourth quarter of 2026.

articles.title: Tata Steel Deploys India's First Coke Oven Gas Injection Technology At Meramandali Plant ...
articles.content: Sep 11, 2026 | Updated 09:22 AM GMT+5:30 Save & read from anywhere! Bookmark stories for easy access on any device or the Swarajya app . Tata Steel commissioned India's first coke oven gas injection project at its Meramandali steel plant in Odisha's Dhenkanal district yesterday (10 September), marking a significant milestone in the country's steel industry. The initiative represents the first deployment of this technology in India and aligns with the company's commitment to achieve Net Zero emissions by 2045. The project enables the blast furnace to operate with a three-fuel system, enhancing operational flexibility whilst reducing dependence on external fossil fuels. Coke oven gas, a hydrogen and hydrocarbon-rich byproduct typically used for power generation or heating, is now being injected directly into Blast Furnace 1 through specialised nozzles called tuyeres, substituting conventional fossil fuels as a reductant. The technology, developed by Paul Wurth-SMS with equipment supplied by Kobelco, can save approximately 0. 65 kilogrammes of coke for each kilogramme of coke oven gas injected. This reduction in coke consumption directly translates to lower carbon dioxide emissions from blast furnace-based ironmaking operations. Tata Steel Meramandali, formerly Bhushan Steel Limited, became part of Tata Steel following its acquisition in 2018 and is recognised as India's largest producer of auto-grade steel. The facility has demonstrated leadership in adopting low-carbon blast furnace technologies, having previously tested coal bed methane, hydrogen, and biochar injection systems. The commissioning strengthens the company's position in sustainable manufacturing by maximising the utilisation of process gases already generated within integrated steel plants. The project combines operational efficiency with environmental gains, offering a productive alternative to simply flaring the gas or using it for conventional heating purposes. articles.title: TCS opens India's first lights-out factory lab in Pune - TechGig
articles.content: AI 1 min read TCS opens India's first lights-out factory lab in Pune Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) has launched India's first lights-out factory lab in Pune to advance AI-first manufacturing. This facility will demonstrate how manufacturing assembly lines can use AI, digital twins, and robotics for automated operations. TechGig Updated On Sep 11, 2026 at 04:59 AM IST Copy Link Share on WhatsApp Share on Linkedin Share on X Share on Telegram Share on Facebook Highlights TCS launched India's first lights-out factory lab in Pune for AI-first manufacturing. The lab integrates AI, digital twins, robotics, and factory control systems for automation. It demonstrates autonomous operations via a fully robotic battery pack assembly line. Manufacturers can prototype and validate AI-first production systems to de-risk deployment. Tata Consultancy Services ( TCS ) has launched the TCS Industrial Autonomy & Engineering Lab – Lights-Out Factory , at its Sahyadri Park campus in Pune. This facility marks India’s maiden lights-out factory lab, designed to simulate and demonstrate how self-optimising factories can automate operations using the TCS Human+AI Service Autonomy Model. The Pune lab integrates digital twins, robotics , industrial AI, factory control systems, and real-time operational intelligence to seamlessly combine technologies for live manufacturing environments. It features a fully robotic battery pack assembly line, showcasing the principles of lights-out manufacturing with minimal human intervention. Advt Addressing Industry 4.0 Challenges The facility aims to help manufacturers prototype, validate, and scale AI-first production systems through simulations on its live setup. It addresses the critical challenge manufacturers face in translating Industry 4.0, AI, and robotics concepts into practical operating models by providing a controlled environment to assess industrial scenarios and reduce deployment risks. The lab supports a range of industry use cases, including predictive maintenance, automated quality inspection, real-time process optimisation, human-machine collaboration, and autonomous factory operations. It focuses on interconnected capabilities such as AI-enabled production optimisation, digital twin and simulation environments for validating factory scenarios, vision AI, robotics for adaptive workflows, and sensor-to-cloud industrial intelligence for real-time decision-making. Sreenivasa Chakravarti, Global Head & Vice President of Industrial Autonomy and Engineering, TCS, stated, "At TCS, we are reimagining those environments and building factories for the future. With our state-of-the-art TCS Industrial Autonomy & Engineering Lab – Lights-Out Factory, we are advancing TCS' vision of engineering AI-first production systems." Advt This initiative is part of TCS' broader work in industrial autonomy, smart manufacturing, engineering transformation, and AI-led enterprise modernisation. Earlier this year, TCS also launched the TCS Industrial Autonomy & Engineering Lab Powered by NVIDIA in Bengaluru to accelerate Physical AI innovation. articles.title: TCS Launches India's First Lights-Out Factory Lab in Pune For AI -Powered Manufacturing
articles.content: Fully Automated Factory Lab Opens at Sahyadri Park Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) has launched India’s first lights-out factory lab at its Sahyadri Park campus in Pune, marking a major step in the company’s push toward AI-led manufacturing and industrial autonomy. A lights-out factory is designed to operate with minimal human intervention , using autonomous systems to run and optimise production processes. TCS says the new facility will allow manufacturers to test these technologies in a controlled environment before deploying them in real factories. Robotic Battery Pack Assembly Line At the centre of the Pune facility is a fully robotic battery pack assembly line with multiple stages of production. The live setup allows manufacturers to prototype, validate and scale AI-first production systems while identifying potential problems before committing to large-scale deployment. This approach could help companies reduce the risks and costs associated with introducing advanced automation directly into operational factories. AI, Robotics and Digital Twins Work Together The lab combines several technologies rather than relying on robotics alone. These include digital twins, industrial AI, factory control systems, Vision AI, robotics and real-time operational intelligence . Digital twins allow manufacturers to create virtual representations of production environments and test different scenarios before making changes to physical equipment. Meanwhile, AI and sensors can analyse shop-floor data and help optimise operations in real time. From Predictive Maintenance to Quality Checks TCS says the facility will support several industrial applications, including predictive maintenance, automated quality inspection, real-time process optimisation, human-machine collaboration and autonomous factory operations . The combination could allow factories to identify equipment problems earlier, detect manufacturing defects automatically and adjust production processes based on real-time conditions. The lab also incorporates sensor-to-cloud industrial intelligence, connecting shop-floor signals with edge and cloud platforms. Helping Manufacturers Test Before Deployment One of the main purposes of the facility is to address a common challenge in industrial transformation: moving from individual automation projects to integrated AI-powered operations. Manufacturers can use the lab to assess Industry 4.0 technologies and determine how suitable they are for particular production environments before making expensive investments. TCS describes this as part of its Human + AI Service Autonomy Model , in which enterprises can gradually move from digitally enabled operations toward increasingly autonomous production systems. TCS Expands Physical AI Push The Pune facility builds on TCS’s broader work in industrial autonomy and physical AI. Earlier in 2026, the company launched an Industrial Autonomy & Engineering Lab powered by NVIDIA in Bengaluru, focused on physical AI applications for industrial and mobility sectors. The Pune lab adds a practical manufacturing environment where these technologies can be demonstrated on a functioning production line. Manufacturing Moves Towards AI-First Operations The development comes as manufacturers increasingly look beyond traditional automation towards systems that can perceive conditions, make decisions and adapt production processes. TCS’s new facility is intended to provide a bridge between AI experimentation and real-world industrial deployment, giving companies a way to test autonomous manufacturing concepts before implementing them at scale. articles.title: ISRO Tests Uprated CE20 Engine, Boosting LVM3 Payload Capacity - Kalinga TV
articles.content: ISRO Tests Uprated CE20 Engine, Boosting LVM3 Payload Capacity ISRO's CE20 engine achieves a historic flight acceptance test at 220 kN, enhancing capabilities for upcoming missions. By KalingaTV Bureau On Sep 10, 2026 Share Advertisement New Delhi: The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) successfully conducted a flight acceptance hot test of its CE20 cryogenic engine at uprated thrust conditions of 220 kN, advancing efforts to enhance the payload capability of the LVM3 launch vehicle and supporting the Gaganyaan programme. The test was conducted on September 9 at the ISRO Propulsion Complex (IPRC) in Mahendragiri, Tamil Nadu, ISRO said on Thursday. In a post on X, the space agency said, “Flight acceptance hot test of CE20 cryogenic engine earmarked for the C32 upper stage of upcoming LVM3 mission at uprated thrust conditions of 220kN is successfully carried out at ISRO Propulsion Complex, Mahendragiri on September 09, 2026.” ISRO also said the performance of the LOX Tank Pressurisation Module (LTPM), intended for the C32 stages of the Gaganyaan missions, was successfully demonstrated during the test. The CE20 engine powers the upper cryogenic stage of the LVM3 launch vehicle. The space agency has been working to operate future LVM3 missions with an uprated C32 stage using the CE20 engine at 22-tonne thrust to enhance the vehicle’s payload capability. The latest test follows a sea-level hot test of the CE20 engine conducted in March at the Mahendragiri facility at the 22-tonne thrust level. The test was carried out using a Nozzle Protection System and a multi-element igniter. Advertisement The March test was aimed at qualifying the engine for sea-level testing at the higher thrust level. ISRO had said the engine and test facility performed as expected during the 165-second test. The CE20’s high-area-ratio nozzle makes sea-level testing particularly challenging because of its low exit pressure. ISRO has noted that flow separation inside the nozzle can cause severe vibrations and thermal stresses, potentially affecting the nozzle’s structural integrity. The latest successful flight acceptance test marks another step towards operationalising the uprated C32 stage for upcoming LVM3 missions. The development also comes shortly after ISRO successfully launched the Advanced Earth Observation Satellite-05 (EOS-05) aboard the GSLV-F17 from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota on September 5. ISRO Chairman V Narayanan had described the mission as a significant achievement, noting that the 2,367-kg satellite was successfully placed in its intended orbit. He said the satellite would become India’s first dedicated imaging satellite from geosynchronous orbit once operationalised.
